keywords.projects: Extra search words (space-separated) that find the project commands. Not shown.
keywords.actions: Extra search words (space-separated) for the Actions group. Not shown.
keywords.ask: Extra search words (space-separated) that find the Ask commands. Not shown.
actions.viewSource: Opens the GitHub repository this website is built from.
actions.openCv: Keep "PDF" as written; CV is the curriculum vitae (résumé).
ask.option: Last row of the palette when the visitor has typed something: choosing it sends what they typed as a question. "Claude" is a product name (the AI model) — never translate it. {query} is exactly what they typed, in any language. Keep the quotation marks appropriate to your language.
ask.suggestions.strongest: A ready-made question a visitor can send with one key. "He" is the site owner, Muhammad.
ask.suggestions.stack: A ready-made question. "He" is the site owner.
ask.suggestions.experience: A ready-made question. "He" is the site owner.
ask.placeholder: Hint inside the question field; ends with an ellipsis. Keep the name Muhammad.
ask.back: Shown after "esc ·" on a small key hint: pressing Escape goes back to the command list. One short word, lower case.
ask.thinking: Shown for a second or two while the answer is being written.
ask.ready: Read aloud to screen-reader users when the answer has finished arriving.
ask.disclaimer: Always visible under every answer. "Claude" is a product name — never translate it. Must say plainly that the answer is generated and can be wrong.
ask.errors.budget: The feature has used its daily allowance and is paused until tomorrow. Friendly, not technical.
ask.errors.rateLimited: The visitor asked many questions in a short time. Friendly, not scolding.
keywords.fit: Extra search words (space-separated) that find the job-fit command. Not shown.
ask.suggestions.live: A ready-made question. "He" is the site owner.
ask.meta: Provenance line under an answer. {facts} is how many facts the answer was grounded on; {steps} how many live data checks ran; {seconds} is already formatted (e.g. 3.9); {model} is a model name like claude-haiku-5.5 — never translate it. Keep it terse, separated by middle dots.
ask.live: Short badge on a source that came from live data fetched just now. One word, lower case.
ask.trace.plan: Label before a sentence the AI wrote about what it was about to do. One short word.
ask.trace.snapshot: Appended when live data could not be fetched and a stored copy was used instead.
ask.trace.get_github_activity.done: Placeholders are raw counts; keep the plural branches (add your language's plural categories).
ask.trace.get_project_progress.done: {overall} is a percentage without the % sign.
ask.trace.get_current_work.done: Placeholders are raw counts; keep the plural branches (add your language's plural categories).
ask.sourceLabels.site: A source pointing to the facts about how this very website was engineered.
fit.command: A palette command: the recruiter pastes a job description and the AI checks each requirement against the site owner's experience. "his" is the site owner.
fit.summary: {strong}, {partial} and {gap} are already-formatted counts of requirements in each verdict. Must match the three verdict words.
fit.verdicts.gap: The verdict when the website does not mention a requirement at all. It must NOT mean "missing", "no" or "fails": it means not shown on this site. Short (one or two words).
fit.verdicts.partial: Related or adjacent evidence only. Short.
fit.verdicts.strong: Directly evidenced by the site. Short.
fit.disclaimer: Always visible under the results. "Claude" is a product name — never translate it. Must keep both points: a gap is not a lack of ability, and the output can be wrong.
fit.shortcut: {key} is ⌘ or Ctrl. Keep "Enter" as the name of the key in your locale.
ask.start: A row in the command list that opens an empty Ask conversation for the visitor to type their own question into. Claude is a product name; keep it.
ask.resume: A row in the command list that reopens the visitor's last Ask conversation. {title} is that conversation's first question, in the visitor's words; keep the quotation marks your language uses.
ask.chat.sidebar: Heading of the sidebar listing the visitor's Ask conversations (like a chat app's history), and the label of the button that shows it on phones.
ask.chat.newChat: Button: start a new, empty conversation. Also shown as the header title before the first question.
ask.chat.fit: Sidebar button that opens the job-description fit check. Keep it short (sidebar is ~200px wide).
ask.chat.commands: Sidebar button that goes back to the command list (the ⌘K palette). The conversation is kept.
ask.chat.noChats: Empty state of the conversation sidebar.
ask.chat.turns: Under each conversation in the sidebar: how many questions it holds.
ask.chat.introTitle: Heading of an empty conversation. Muhammad is the site owner; use the transliteration in Common.owner.
ask.chat.introBody: Text under that heading. 'below' refers to the input field at the bottom.
ask.chat.tryAsking: Small uppercase label over the starter questions.
ask.chat.followupPlaceholder: Placeholder of the input once a conversation has started.
ask.chat.send: Accessible name of the send button (an arrow icon).
ask.chat.stop: Accessible name of the button that stops an answer while it is being written.
ask.chat.stopped: Shown under an answer the visitor stopped part way.
